pigeon:
I left three white feathers by the late night train
The station clock clicked and my crew came again.

A baker dropped a bag by the edge of the square
I shook out a banquet and took to the air.

I counted every window from the top of the dome
You called it a skyline and I called it home.

I made a bass drum out of one old street sign
The bus took a turn and the echo was mine.

My toes caught a tremor on the rim of the roof
The glass rang twice and the whole flock had proof.

I ducked under canvas and dined on a chip
Your band took a break and my wings took a trip.

I drew a thin shadow down the length of the street
It curved at the corner and landed on beat.

A bell struck seven and I sailed past the clock
My breakfast was waiting a roof down the block.

I took a small crumb to the top of the spire
The wind got louder and the hook went higher.

The old weathervane pointed west at the rain
I turned to the east and started up again.

A busker packed up with a bow and a grin
I carried the tune to the edge of the inn.

I rode the warm air past the bricks of the bank
You waited downstairs and the whole chorus sank.
disco-ball:
The dancers went quiet when the room lost its glow
I caught a small beam and sent it back in a row.

My mirrors put a path up the wallpaper seam
The crowd found the groove in the bend of the beam.
raccoon:
I folded a drum stand from a rusty old grate
The hinges kept time till a quarter past eight.

I borrowed a handle from a battered tin pail
The lid gave a crack and my coat caught the hail.
librarian:
I left you a note on the page with the fold
The missing citation was worth more than gold.

I read your whole claim with a lamp at my desk
One line in the margin did more than the rest.
weather-forecaster:
The north wind changed when the bass came through
My chart caught a drop at a quarter past two.

I drew a long arrow from the coast to the hall
The rain went around and the leaves took the fall.

pigeon:
The grocer put a bag on the bench in the sun
I counted the crumbs till the whole job was done.

I heard a brass band under canvas at noon
I flew by the trumpet and borrowed its tune.

I tapped out a beat on the lip of a drain
The roof threw it back like a drum made of rain.
disco-ball:
My silver squares scattered a stripe across the room
The last pair danced through the edge of the gloom.
raccoon:
I found a bass note in a black plastic drum
The alley stood still and the whole block came.
librarian:
I brought back the book with a strip of blue tape
Your favorite excuse had escaped from the page.
weather-forecaster:
The fog cleared a path to the edge of the bay
My report came in just as it faded away.

The bricks were below me and so were the trees.

I dropped that {cue} on a street full of snow
The flurry took over and finished the show.

Your {cue} made a claim by the side of the train
I rode on the wind and was home before rain.

I left that {cue} at the base of a spire
The ledge took my feet and my verse climbed higher.

I sent that {cue} to the end of the block
My beak kept time with the old city clock.

That {cue} took a bow on a neat strip of grass

I watched that {cue} from the top of the gate

I held that {cue} in the shade of a tent

I set that {cue} on a ledge in the sun

That {cue} went cold by the side of the lake

I found that {cue} where the balconies meet

I sent that {cue} round the back of a dome

I heard that {cue} in the mouth of an alley

I kept that {cue} off the tip of my wing

I put that {cue} on a sign in the square

Your {cue} missed the turn at the top of the hill

That {cue} hit a stone at the edge of the bay

I left that {cue} with the crowd at the bar
My feet hit the gutter and rang from afar.

Your {cue} tried a turn on a wet copper rail
I curved on the wind without moving my tail.

I watched that {cue} from a ledge in the heat

I led that {cue} on a chase past the park
My crew stayed quiet and the street went dark.

I took that {cue} to the top of a mast
A gust went by slowly and I passed it fast.

That {cue} put a price on a place by the door
I flew to the rafters and never paid more.

The dots took a turn and came back down the hall.

I put that {cue} in a bright little ring

I put that {cue} on the map by the pier
